'''Riccardo Barbieri''' (born 1944) is an Italian theoretical physicist and a professor at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa]]. He has written more than two hundred research papers in the field of theoretical elementary particle physics,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://inspirehep.net/author/R.Barbieri.1|title = Inspire}}</ref> and has been particularly influential in [[physics beyond the Standard Model]].

==Research career==

Riccardo Barbieri received his undergraduate education from 1963 to 1967 at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore]] in Pisa and at the [[University of Pisa]]. His ''laurea'' advisor was [[Pietro Menotti]]. During his professionalization classes (''perfezionamento'') from 1967 to 1969 at the Scuola Normale Superiore and in later years he worked on higher-order radiative corrections in [[Quantum Electrodynamics]] with [[Ettore Remiddi]]. In the 1970s, he turned to computations in [[Quantum Chromodynamics]], collaborating in particular with [[:it:Raoul Gatto|Raoul Gatto]] and [[Zoltan Kunszt]]. In 1976 at [[CERN]], he made the prediction, later experimentally verified, of the hadronic widths of the three [[charmonium]] P-waves.<ref>{{Cite journal
| doi = 10.1016/0370-2693(76)90419-6
| issn = 0370-2693
| volume = 60
| issue = 2
| pages = 183–188
| last = Barbieri
| first = R.
| author2=R. Gatto |author3=R. Kögerler
| title = Calculation of the annihilation rate of P wave quark-antiquark bound states
| journal = Physics Letters B
| year = 1976
| url = https://cds.cern.ch/record/697006/files/197512076.pdf
| bibcode = 1976PhLB...60..183B
}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal
| doi = 10.1016/0370-2693(76)90729-2
| issn = 0370-2693
| volume = 61
| issue = 5
| pages = 465–468
| last = Barbieri
| first = R.
| author2=R. Gatto |author3=E. Remiddi
| title = Singular binding dependence in the hadronic widths of 1++ and 1+− heavy quark antiquark bound states
| journal = Physics Letters B
| year = 1976
| url = http://inspirehep.net/record/108193?ln=en
| bibcode = 1976PhLB...61..465B
| url-access = subscription
}}</ref>

From 1980 to 1982, Riccardo Barbieri was a staff member at the [[CERN]] Theory Division. The [[Standard Model]] of particle physics by then well established, he started focussing on models [[Physics beyond the Standard Model|beyond the Standard Model]], in particular [[supersymmetry]]. In 1982, he formulated the first realistic model of mediation of supersymmetry breaking via supergravity.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Riccardo Barbieri |author2=Sergio Ferrara |author3=Calos Savoy |title= Gauge Models with Spontaneously Broken Local Supersymmetry|journal= Phys. Lett. B|volume= 119|issue=4–6 |pages=343–347|year= 1982|doi= 10.1016/0370-2693(82)90685-2|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/139226 |bibcode=1982PhLB..119..343B }}</ref>

Since 1984 and until now, Riccardo Barbieri has been the professor of theoretical physics at Pisa, first at the [[University of Pisa]] (1984–97), and then at the Scuola Normale Superiore (1998–present). Some of his most influential results in this period include: 
* In 1988, the quantitative formulation of the naturalness concept in supersymmetric models.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Riccardo Barbieri |author2=Gian F. Giudice |title= Upper Bounds on Supersymmetric Particle Masses|journal=Nucl. Phys. B|volume= 306|issue=1 |pages=63–76|year= 1988|doi= 10.1016/0550-3213(88)90171-X|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/180560 |bibcode=1988NuPhB.306...63B }}</ref>
* In 1990, the formulation of a reference parametrization of the quantum corrections to the electroweak precision observables.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Riccardo Barbieri |author2=Guido Altarelli |title= Vacuum polarization effects of new physics on electroweak processes |journal= Phys. Lett. B|volume= 253|issue=1–2 |pages=161–167|year= 1991|doi= 10.1016/0370-2693(91)91378-9|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/212333 |bibcode=1991PhLB..253..161A }}</ref>
* In 1995, pointing out the significance of flavour and CP violations in supersymmetric unified theories even in the absence of any flavour or CP violation in the input for the soft-supersymmetry breaking parameters.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Riccardo Barbieri |author2=Lawrence J. Hall |author3=Alessandro Strumia |title= Violations of lepton flavor and CP in supersymmetric unified theories|journal=Nucl. Phys. B|volume= 405|issue=2–3 |pages=219–251|year= 1995|doi= 10.1016/0550-3213(95)00208-A|arxiv=hep-ph/9501334|bibcode=1995NuPhB.445..219B |s2cid=14445005 }}</ref>
* In 2006, the proposal of a Dark Matter model based on a second Higgs doublet without vacuum expectation value.<ref>{{Cite journal
| doi = 10.1103/PhysRevD.74.015007
| volume = 74
| issue = 1
| article-number = 015007
| last = Barbieri
| first = Riccardo
| author2=Lawrence Hall |author3=Vyacheslav Rychkov
| title = Improved naturalness with a heavy Higgs boson: An alternative road to CERN LHC physics
| journal = Physical Review D
| year = 2006
| url = http://inspirehep.net/record/713004?ln=en
| arxiv = hep-ph/0603188
| bibcode = 2006PhRvD..74a5007B
| s2cid = 15412955
}}</ref>

==Mentoring==

Having taught in Pisa for 30 years, Riccardo Barbieri is acclaimed for creating a school of theoretical high-energy physics. Among many of his students and postdocs who went on to become professors of theoretical physics in Italy and around the world, are [[Gian F. Giudice]], and [[Michelangelo Mangano]] (permanent staff members at the [[CERN]]), Giovanni Ridolfi (professor at the [[University of Genoa]]), [[Riccardo Rattazzi]] (professor at the [[EPFL]]), [[Francesco Vissani]] (INFN director of research at [[Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso]]), [[Alessandro Strumia]] (professor at the [[University of Pisa]]), [[Andrea Romanino]] (professor at [[SISSA]]), [[Roberto Contino]] (professor at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]]), [[Paolo Creminelli]] (professor at the [[ICTP]]), [[Michele Papucci]] (Divisional Fellow at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]]), [[Gia Dvali]] (professor at the [[LMU Munich]]), [[Vyacheslav Rychkov]] (professor at the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques|IHES]]), [[Stefania Gori]] (professor at UC Santa Cruz).

==Awards and honours==

Prof. Barbieri was awarded the "Ordine del Cherubino" from the University of Pisa in 1997, the Humboldt Prize and, more recently, the Physics Prize of "Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei" in 2017. He was also a Miller Visiting Professor at the University of California, Berkeley.
